text:
maria: Quick share — ran continuous-batcher sweep across us-west (h100), eu-west (a100), ap-south (h100-small). Results below. TL;DR: us-west has best p95 but ap-south shows p99 spikes with current batch_window_ms=12 + max_batch_tokens=2048. Thoughts on kernel overrides and fairness tuning?

bench-bot: run 1954327890/summary
us-west/h100: p50=9ms p75=16ms p95=34ms p99=110ms throughput=850 tok/s
eu-west/a100: p50=12ms p75=22ms p95=48ms p99=140ms throughput=720 tok/s
ap-south/h100-small: p50=14ms p75=26ms p95=60ms p99=420ms throughput=410 tok/s
config: batch_window_ms=12 max_batch_tokens=2048 scheduler=continuous fairshare=on kernels=[attn-fused-v1]

kevin: That APAC p99 looks like microburst tail — probably tiny cohort sizes + kernel fallback to unfused when seq_len>512. Saw the same pattern last month.

priya: Can we try batch_window_ms=6 and max_batch_tokens=1024 and allowlist kernels [attn-fused-v2, attn-fused-v1]? v2 has better long-seq memory locality so fewer fallbacks.

jun: Also include quantization variants — fp16 vs q4_0. Quant changes KV cache insert timing and can amplify the tail. Proposed sweep: kernels x {q4_0,q8_0,fp16} x batch_window_ms {6,12,24} x max_batch_tokens {1024,2048} per-region.

kevin: +1. And if fairness is enabled, pin cohort weights (small/medium/large) for APAC, otherwise continuous batcher tends to tilt toward large requests and starve small ones on smaller hardware.

maria: Plan: bench-bot to kick off Jun's grid, with per-region kernel allowlist and cohort pinning. I'll own ap-south followups. Assignments: @bench-bot enqueue, @jun define the grid, @priya kernel whitelist, @kevin cohort pinning config.

bench-bot: acknowledged. enqueue 36 jobs. ETA ~3h. Will post a condensed table + charts in this thread when done :robot_face:

maria: Please capture seq_len buckets: <=128, 129-512, 513+. We need p50/p75/p95/p99 per bucket so we can correlate kernel fallback thresholds.

priya: Noted — adding seq_len bucketing and kernel-level logs (kernel_selected + reason).

kevin: If APAC still shows tail after the sweep, consider region-specific batch_window jitter (random 0..X ms) to smooth synchronized arrivals. Also check NIC interrupts and small-cohort placement.

maria: Great. I'll schedule a 30m results sync tomorrow 10am PT. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
